item.title: Ars Biologica ArtXScience Residency 2027-2028 (Ars Electronica x Ceske Budejovice ECoC 2028)
item.description:
Organisation: Ars Electronica and Ceske Budejovice - European Capital of Culture 2028

Location: Ceske Budejovice, Czech Republic. Open to applicants of any nationality aged 18+ who are legally eligible to work and travel in the EU. Required on-site stays: up to one month in February/March 2027, an optional stay in August/September 2027, and March 2028 for installation, exhibition and deinstallation.

Award: EUR 24,000 total package per winner: EUR 6,000 artist fee, up to EUR 15,000 production budget, and up to EUR 3,000 for travel, accommodation and subsistence, plus a separate budget covering one month of housing in Ceske Budejovice. Two positions available. Free to apply.

Duration: January 2027 to April 2028, with on-site blocks in early 2027 and March 2028

Deadline: 28 Sep 2026

A fully funded art-science residency from Ars Electronica and Ceske Budejovice, European Capital of Culture 2028, exploring how art and science can collaborate on urgent environmental challenges: climate emergence, sustainable agriculture, geoengineering, permaculture, water resource management, and the broader ecological impacts on local communities. Selected residents work in direct collaboration with local scientists in Ceske Budejovice. WHO CAN APPLY: artists, designers, creatives and artist collectives with more than 5 years of professional creative practice and documented interdisciplinary work; experience in community engagement and science collaborations is essential; applicants must be 18+, of any nationality, and legally eligible to work and travel in the EU. WHAT YOU GET: a EUR 24,000 package (EUR 6,000 artist fee, up to EUR 15,000 production, up to EUR 3,000 travel and subsistence) plus one month of housing covered separately; two winners are selected. STRUCTURE: the residency runs January 2027 to April 2028, with a required on-site stay of up to one month in February/March 2027, an optional stay in August/September 2027, and a March 2028 stay for festival installation, exhibition and deinstallation. HOW TO APPLY: online form with project title, a written proposal of max 250 words, a scientific direction statement (max 100 words), artistic vision (max 100 words), community connection plan (max 100 words), a super short pitch (3 to 30 words), 3 to 7 images, an optional 1-minute video, a portfolio link and contact information. Two-round selection (online application then interview); winners notified by November 2026. Deadline 28 September 2026 at midnight CET.

item.title: Perform Europe: Third Open Call for Cross-Border Touring (2026-28 edition)
item.description:
Organisation: Perform Europe (IETM, EFA, Circostrada, European Dancehouse Network, Pearle*, IDEA Consult), co-funded by Creative Europe

Location: Europe-wide; touring must happen in at least 3 Creative Europe countries. The UK is NOT eligible.

Award: Three grant tiers of EUR 15,000, EUR 25,000 or EUR 55,000, plus top-ups of up to EUR 5,000, giving a EUR 60,000 ceiling per partnership. EUR 1.4 million total across at least 25 partnerships, covering up to 100 percent of eligible costs, so no matching funds are needed. TOP-UP RATES: green mobility EUR 400 per person per presentation date; accessibility support EUR 400 per person per presentation date; family top-up EUR 200 per child per presentation date; audience access EUR 800 per presentation date; visa EUR 120 per person needing one; overseas and outermost regions EUR 175 per person per presentation date. No application fee.

Duration: Touring and implementation 1 March 2027 to 31 January 2028 (11 months).

Deadline: 22 Oct 2026

Perform Europe is the EU's dedicated cross-border touring scheme for the performing arts, run by a six-organisation consortium and co-funded by Creative Europe. It funds partnerships of at least three organisations from three different Creative Europe countries to tour a finished performing arts work in at least three countries, with an explicit emphasis on greener, more inclusive and more equitable touring practice. Eligible disciplines are circus, dance, outdoor arts, performance art, puppetry and theatre; LIVE MUSIC AND OPERA ARE EXCLUDED, and production costs for new creations are not covered since the work must already be finished before 1 March 2027. Applicants pick one of three grant tiers with no fixed criteria per tier, and may request up to EUR 5,000 in top-ups for accessibility and sustainability measures. Five percent of the total fund is ring-fenced for proposals involving Ukrainian partners or supporting the Ukrainian performing arts sector. All 41 Creative Europe countries are eligible, including Albania, Armenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Iceland, Kosovo, Liechtenstein, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Norway, Serbia, Tunisia and Ukraine, but the UK is not. TIMING: applications close 22 October 2026 at 23:59 CEST, selected partnerships are announced in January 2027, and activity may only start from 1 March 2027. A Matchmaking Platform with over 2,300 registered professionals is available for finding partners before applying. CORE PRIORITY: each partnership must pick either diversity and inclusion or the fight against climate change as its core priority, and must also include measures addressing the other one; that choice has to run visibly through the whole application rather than sit in one section. WHO COUNTS AS A PARTNER: both organisations and individual professionals are eligible, so a partner can be an artist, collective, company, producer, presenter, venue, festival, residency, educational institution or NGO. Eligibility is decided by where you are legally based. The partnership appoints a lead partner who submits, signs and receives the grant. ELIGIBLE COSTS: artistic fees and salaries, travel, accommodation, subsistence, administration, reporting, communication, translation, surtitling, equipment transport, copyright fees, access and environmental measures, complementary activities and capacity building. Venue and equipment rental or purchase is capped at 5 percent of the requested grant, and preparation costs for presenting an existing work at 10 percent. PAYMENT: 60 percent after signing, 20 percent after the first narrative and financial report is approved, and the final 20 percent after completion and EU approval of Perform Europe's own final report. Top-ups are reimbursed only after the project ends and documentation is approved, so budget for the cash-flow gap. PRACTICAL: every partner must register for a Perform Europe account before submission and approval can take several working days, so do not leave that to the last week.

item.title: Fonds BJP: Dossiersubsidie for Freelance Regional and Local Journalists (autumn 2026 round)
item.description:
Organisation: Fonds Bijzondere Journalistieke Projecten (Fonds BJP)

Location: Netherlands; for freelance journalists working on Dutch regional and local reporting

Award: Up to EUR 19,200 for six months of work on a single reporting dossier. No application fee.

Duration: Six months of dedicated reporting on one subject area

Deadline: 14 Sep 2026

The Dossiersubsidie is the Fonds BJP scheme for freelance regional and local journalists in the Netherlands who want to follow one subject properly rather than chase daily news, funding up to EUR 19,200 for six months of sustained reporting on a single dossier. It is aimed at the gap left by shrinking regional newsrooms, where structural coverage of local government, housing, care or industry rarely gets paid time. ELIGIBILITY: freelance journalists working in Dutch regional and local media only (staff journalists and national-only reporters are directed to the fund's other schemes). The fund also runs a year-round Vooronderzoekssubsidie of up to EUR 8,800 for preliminary research and a year-round Uitvoeringssubsidie of up to EUR 38,600 for carrying out projects, both open to all journalists. APPLICATION WINDOW: 17 August to 14 September 2026, via the Fonds BJP subsidy portal. Online office hours on 8 September 2026; questions on 020 63 86 295.

item.title: Programme PAUSE: Emergency Hosting for Scientists and Artists in Exile (autumn 2026 call)
item.description:
Organisation: Programme PAUSE, hosted by the College de France, with the French Ministries of Higher Education and Research and of Culture

Location: France (hosting at a French higher education, research or cultural institution)

Award: PAUSE co-funds the hosting project (salary and support costs) together with the host institution; amounts depend on the project and institution. No application fee.

Duration: Hosting periods are typically 12 months, renewable subject to review

Deadline: 24 Sep 2026

PAUSE is the French national programme for the emergency hosting of scientists and artists in exile, created in 2017 and run from the College de France. It co-funds a stay at a French higher education or research establishment or at a cultural institution so that a researcher, doctoral candidate or artist at risk can keep working, and it also supports their family. ELIGIBILITY: applicants must be able to prove status as a doctoral student (with a thesis in progress interrupted by the emergency), researcher, teacher-researcher or artist-teacher in their country of origin; must be in a crisis situation because of the security situation in that country or because of persecution or fear of persecution on grounds of ethnicity, religion, political convictions, opinions or sexual orientation, or the content of their research or teaching; and must be forced into exile or have been in France for less than three years. HOST REQUIREMENT: a French host institution is mandatory and submits the application; eligible hosts are institutions under the French higher education and research ministry, EESPIG private institutions, and structures supported by the Ministry of Culture. PAUSE publishes a list of at-risk candidates looking for a host, which institutions can use to find a match. The call opens at the end of August 2026 with a deadline of 24 September 2026.

item.title: Stimuleringsfonds: Open Call Residency Videotage 2027 (Hong Kong)
item.description:
Organisation: Stimuleringsfonds Creatieve Industrie (Creative Industries Fund NL) in collaboration with Videotage, Hong Kong

Location: Residency takes place at Videotage in Hong Kong. Applicants must be established in the Netherlands, Aruba, Bonaire, Curacao, Saba, Sint Eustatius or Sint Maarten (Kingdom of the Netherlands) and registered in a business register within the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

Award: EUR 5,000 for a two-month residency or EUR 6,500 for a three-month residency, paid by the Creative Industries Fund NL to cover travel, insurance, living expenses, compensation for time invested, and material and transport costs. Accommodation, use of the studio space and facilitation by Videotage are covered directly by the Fund on top of this. No application fee.

Duration: Two or three months in 2027 (spring 2027); state your preferred period in the application.

Deadline: 21 Oct 2026

The Creative Industries Fund NL (Stimuleringsfonds) runs this residency with Videotage, a Hong Kong-based non-profit media arts institution specialising in the promotion, presentation, creation and preservation of moving image and media art in all forms and languages. The Fund is recruiting one Netherlands-based designer, maker or observer working in digital culture to spend two or three months at Videotage's studio space in Hong Kong in 2027, conducting research, broadening their network, developing new work inspired by Hong Kong, and presenting their findings or completed works. The residency encourages crossovers and experimentation, giving the participant space to explore new methodologies, widen their creative practice and produce work that pushes the boundaries of digital culture, with a focus on social and urban dynamics. The 2027 edition takes the technological 'black box' phenomenon as its starting point and invites the resident to respond to that theme within the context of Videotage. ELIGIBILITY: you are an individual designer, maker or observer within the field of digital culture; you are established in the Netherlands, Aruba, Bonaire, Curacao, Saba, Sint Eustatius or Sint Maarten (Kingdom of the Netherlands); you are registered in the business register of the Dutch Chamber of Commerce (KvK) or another business register within the Kingdom of the Netherlands; and you have had a professional practice in the creative industry for at least four years. NOT open to duos, collectives or cooperative ventures, nor to designers and makers who receive a grant during the work period under the Talent Development Grant Scheme, the Open Call Self-taught Designer or the Open Call Emerging Design Practices ABCSSS. Note that accepting this open call means you cannot apply to those schemes and open calls in 2027. FUNDING: EUR 5,000 for two months or EUR 6,500 for three months, covering travel, insurance, living expenses, compensation for time invested and material and transport costs; accommodation, studio use and Videotage's facilitation are covered separately by the Fund. Submit your proposal to the Creative Industries Fund NL by 21 October 2026, 16:00 CEST.

item.title: Statens Kunstfond: Production and Exhibitions, Contemporary Art in Denmark and Abroad (2026 autumn round)
item.description:
Organisation: Statens Kunstfond (Danish Arts Foundation)

Location: Denmark and abroad. Non-Danish venues and organisations may apply, but only for exhibitions that feature Danish artists.

Award: DKK. No published minimum or maximum; the committee assesses each application on its merits and historical awards are published on the site. No stated co-financing requirement. No application fee. Applications must be submitted digitally via the Danish subsidy portal (Tilskudsportalen).

Duration: Project-length; production and exhibition periods vary.

Deadline: 24 Sep 2026

The Danish Arts Foundation's Production and Exhibitions programme funds the production, dissemination and exhibition of contemporary art in Denmark and abroad, and it is one of the few Nordic national schemes a foreign organisation can apply to directly. Eligible costs include creating new works where an exhibition agreement is in place, exhibition costs, exhibition programming featuring Danish or international artists, promotion tied to an exhibition, and honorariums covering artists' work and installation time, which lets a festival or biennial cover commission and artist-fee lines. THE KEY CONDITION for non-Danish applicants is that the exhibition must feature Danish artists; Danish artists and venues face no such restriction. No minimum or maximum grant is published since the committee decides case by case, and previous award levels are visible on the site. Two 2026 deadlines apply: 26 March 2026 (closed) and 24 September 2026 at 14:00, with the application form opening one month before each deadline. TIMING: applicants receive a response no later than twelve weeks after the deadline, so expect a decision by mid-December 2026. Applications must go through the Danish digital subsidy portal; submissions outside it are rejected except in very special circumstances. FLAG: earliest-start-date rules are not specified on the funder's page.

item.title: Fonds Darstellende Kuenste: GLOBAL VILLAGE KIDS im digitalen Raum (2026 round)
item.description:
Organisation: Fonds Darstellende Kuenste e.V.

Location: Germany. All coalition members must be based in Germany, though non-German artists may be involved as contracted artists.

Award: Laboratory projects EUR 5,000 to 15,000; process projects EUR 15,000 to 40,000. Both figures include a 7 percent administrative overhead. Full financing model, no co-financing required. No application fee.

Duration: Earliest start 1 January 2027; projects must conclude by 31 August 2027; final reports due 30 September 2027.

Deadline: 01 Oct 2026

The digital-space strand of the Fonds Darstellende Kuenste GLOBAL VILLAGE KIDS programme, funding format-open and results-open artistic projects and artist-participatory approaches in digital and hybrid performing arts. Eligible artistic fields explicitly include digital performing arts alongside performance, theatre, dance, musical theatre, puppet theatre and contemporary circus, which makes it usable for hybrid or online public programmes. The applicant must be a coalition of at least three legally constituted organisations spanning arts and culture, education and civil society, all German-based, so this is genuinely institution-facing rather than artist-facing; individual artists cannot apply, and schools and kindergartens may participate as partners but cannot be the applying organisation. Two tiers exist: laboratory projects at EUR 5,000 to 15,000 requiring a minimum 30 hours of work, and process projects at EUR 15,000 to 40,000 requiring a minimum 60 hours, both inclusive of a 7 percent administrative fee. FULL FINANCING is available with no matching requirement, which is unusual and valuable. TIMING: the deadline is 1 October 2026 with the earliest permitted project start on 1 January 2027, so the decision lag is roughly three months. Applications go exclusively through the kumasta online database. FIT CAVEAT: the programme targets children and young people aged 3 to 18 in situations of social, financial or educational disadvantage, so it suits a digital-arts programme with a youth participation core rather than a general public festival.

item.title: Fondazione CRT: Bando Ordinarie 2026, Arte, attivita e beni culturali, Progetti (second session)
item.description:
Organisation: Fondazione CRT (Fondazione Cassa di Risparmio di Torino)

Location: Piedmont and Valle d'Aosta, Italy. The project must be delivered in those regions, but the applicant does not need to be headquartered there.

Award: No published fixed minimum or maximum for the arts strand; grant size is set case by case against the project budget and the applicant's financial capacity. Co-financing is not universally mandated but specific categories carry thresholds (conference and seminar requests above EUR 10,000 are inadmissible without co-financing of at least two thirds of budgeted spend). Across all three areas Fondazione CRT distributed roughly EUR 5.5 million to 349 projects in a single recent Ordinarie session. No application fee.

Duration: Project-based; grant-use period governed by the Regolamento Generale di Erogazione 2026, with extensions of up to 12 months available on request.

Deadline: 15 Oct 2026

The Bando Ordinarie is Fondazione CRT's open, non-thematic route: organisations can request support for initiatives that fit the foundation's statutory aims but do not fall under any of its thematic calls, across three areas of which one is Arte, attivita e beni culturali (branded Meraviglia). It is the right door for public programmes, cultural projects, media and digital-culture initiatives and events that are not live performance, exhibitions, film festivals or restoration. READ THE EXCLUSION LIST CAREFULLY: live performance goes to NoteSipari or Orizzonti L.I.V.E., exhibition-format initiatives and film festivals go to Immagini e Prospettive, heritage restoration goes to BeST, and accessible territorial-showcase events go to Eventi for All, so Ordinarie is the residual arts route. Non-profit entities and institutions operating in the reference territory are eligible, and because the applicant does not need to be headquartered in Piedmont or Valle d'Aosta this is genuinely open to organisations based elsewhere, including non-EU and UK, that run a programme in those regions. The project route has two deadlines: the first was 30 April 2026 and the second session is open 1 July to 15 October 2026 at 15:00 Italian time. Organisations receiving an activity-support grant cannot also benefit from other CRT calls in the same calendar year. Applications are made through rol.fondazionecrt.it.

item.title: Martin Roth-Initiative: Temporary Relocation for Artists and Cultural Actors at Risk (Programme Line 1, 2026 call)
item.description:
Organisation: Martin Roth-Initiative (Goethe-Institut and ifa, funded by the German Federal Foreign Office)

Location: Germany (relocation to a German host organisation). Open to artists and cultural actors worldwide, with exclusions.

Award: Monthly scholarship for the relocated artist, plus insurance, language courses, psychosocial support, counselling and training, visa support, and personnel funding for the host organisation. No application fee.

Duration: Up to 15 months, starting no earlier than 15 January 2027

Deadline: 11 Sep 2026

The Martin Roth-Initiative is the German temporary-relocation programme for artists and cultural actors at risk, run jointly by the Goethe-Institut and ifa with Federal Foreign Office funding. Programme Line 1 relocates an artist to Germany for up to 15 months on a scholarship, with insurance, language courses, psychosocial support, counselling and visa assistance, plus personnel funding for the hosting organisation. ELIGIBILITY: artists and cultural practitioners anywhere in the world who are demonstrably committed through their work to an open society, freedom, peace and democracy; who face threats, persecution or unsafe living conditions; who have no access to a safe place to continue working; and who speak English or German. Applicants must still be active in their home country or have left it after 20 February 2026. Citizens of EU and EEA countries, Australia, Canada, Israel, New Zealand, Switzerland, the UK and the USA are excluded, as are residents of Gaza and previous MRI recipients. HOST REQUIREMENT: applications are submitted jointly with a non-profit host organisation in Germany (museum, theatre, festival, cultural collective, NGO) that is a legal entity able to handle the administrative and digital-security requirements. Note that the scholarship visa does not itself permit employment or self-employment in Germany. TIMELINE: applications 6 July to 11 September 2026; decisions end of November 2026; funding starts no earlier than 15 January 2027. Apply to apply@mri-application.de (encrypted email recommended); phone +49 30 284491-77.

item.title: Kulturdirektoratet: Cross-Disciplinary Cultural Activity, Events, Organisers and Venues (2026 autumn round)
item.description:
Organisation: Kulturdirektoratet (Arts and Culture Norway)

Location: Norway. Activity is expected to take place in Norway, though international artists and partners can be programmed.

Award: NOK. No fixed minimum or maximum published; grant sizes are assessed against the project budget, financing plan and available funds. Kulturdirektoratet states it does not provide full financing, so co-financing is required in practice but no fixed percentage is set. Historical award levels are published in the scheme's public decision database. No application fee.

Duration: Project grants for single events or series; activity grants cover the 2027 operating year.

Deadline: 15 Sep 2026

Kulturdirektoratet's main scheme for multi-artistic and cross-disciplinary events, organisers and venues, and the natural Norwegian route for a festival or biennial that does not sit inside a single artform committee. It funds single events, event series, festivals and seminars with cross-disciplinary relevance, plus year-round operation of organisations with a multi-artistic profile, which covers media arts, digital culture and experimental sound programming presented alongside other forms. Art production itself, closed workshops, infrastructure investment and activity already completed before the deadline are not funded. Two application rounds run in 2026: 8 April 2026 (project grants, closed) and 15 September 2026 at 13:00 (project grants plus activity grants for the 2027 operating year). Project grants accept individuals, private and public institutions, and organisations, while activity grants require an organisation number or a named, separately budgeted activity within a larger entity, existing for at least one year and not already receiving permanent annual state funding. The scheme never fully finances a project, so a credible co-financing plan is expected. FLAG: decision dates and foreign-applicant eligibility are not published on the scheme page; award notifications arrive via the application portal.

item.title: Kulturdirektoratet: Arrangorstotte Visuell Kunst, Visual Art Organisers Support (2026 round)
item.description:
Organisation: Kulturdirektoratet (Arts and Culture Norway)

Location: Norway. Foreign applicant eligibility is not stated on the scheme page.

Award: NOK. No published minimum or maximum; award sizes vary with budget and available funds and previous awards are listed in the scheme's decision database. Kulturdirektoratet does not provide full financing, so co-financing is expected and applicants often receive less than requested. No application fee.

Duration: Operating and programme support, typically covering the following activity year.

Deadline: 15 Sep 2026

This scheme gives operating and programme support to visual art organisers in Norway, covering exhibition and event programming, content production, salaries, artist fees, venue costs including rent, utilities and internet, and administrative expenses. Because it funds the organiser rather than a single artwork, it is the relevant route for an artist-run space, biennial organisation or media-arts venue running a recurring public programme. Applicants must demonstrate artistic and cultural expertise, innovation and distinctiveness. Eligibility is limited to bodies with their own registration number, or a separately named and budgeted activity within a larger organisation, existing for at least one year prior to application, and organisations already receiving permanent annual state funding are excluded. The 2026 application deadline is 15 September 2026 at 13:00. Kulturdirektoratet explicitly warns that applicants often receive less than requested or are rejected despite quality proposals, so co-financing is necessary. item.title: Kone Foundation: Annual Grant Call (2026)
item.description:
Organisation: Kone Foundation / Koneen Saatio (Finland)

Location: Finland. Work may be carried out abroad by Finnish citizens. Projects must have a connection to Finland.

Award: Artistic groups and organisations up to EUR 250,000; research groups typically EUR 200,000 to 500,000. Minimum project duration six months for individual applicants and one month for groups; maximum four consecutive years for the same project. No co-financing requirement stated. No application fee. No retroactive funding.

Duration: One month to four years; projects must start in January or later.

Deadline: 15 Sep 2026

Kone Foundation is Finland's major private funder for academic research in the humanities, social sciences and environmental sciences, for professional artistic work across all disciplines, and specifically for multidisciplinary projects combining scholarly and artistic approaches, which is where digital culture, media arts and artistic research proposals land. Individuals, working groups and legal entities with a Finnish business ID may apply, and artistic groups and organisations can receive up to EUR 250,000. The Finland connection is the binding constraint: a non-Finnish applicant needs a Finnish institutional affiliation, Finland residence, or the work must happen in Finland, though international collaborators can join a group freely once one member is a Finnish citizen or Finland-based. Psychology, theology, law, business studies without an interdisciplinary element, and medical research are not funded, nor are master's studies, continuing education, building renovation, standalone equipment purchases or hobby activity. The annual call runs 1 to 15 September each year, closing 15 September 2026 at 16:00 EEST, with decisions announced in November and December. TIMING: funding is never retroactive and projects must begin in January or later, so a September 2026 application funds work starting January 2027 at the earliest. FLAG: Kone frames its funding around artistic work and research projects rather than festival or event hosting as such, so an event-led application needs to be framed as an artistic or research project.

item.title: Utrecht University: PhD, Media and Democracy in the 1970s (NWO Vidi project)
item.description:

Location: Utrecht, Netherlands (Drift 6)

Award: EUR 3,059 to 3,881 gross per month at 36 to 40 hours per week, on the Dutch university PhD scale, plus 8 percent holiday allowance and 8.3 percent year-end bonus. No application fee.

Duration: 18-month initial contract, extended to four years after a positive first-year assessment

Deadline: 06 Sep 2026

Fully funded PhD position in the NWO-funded Vidi project 'Democracy and the (de-)regulation of the media in Europe since the 1970s', which reads the contestation and transformation of democracy in the last quarter of the twentieth century through media governance. This sub-project examines how social movements, pirate broadcasters and alternative media initiatives challenged the public broadcasting monopoly across Western Europe during the long 1970s, drawing on archival research. REQUIREMENTS: a master's degree in history or a related field, a demonstrated interest in the history of democracy and media governance, professional English plus at least one other European language, archival research experience and a collaborative approach. item.title: Studio ALTA Residence 2027: four residency open calls (Prague)
item.description:
Organisation: Studio ALTA

Location: Studio ALTA, Prague (Liben district), Czech Republic. Three of the four calls are open internationally; the Rest House call is reserved for supporting-profession arts workers active in the Czech independent sector.

Award: Residency fees paid to participants: Research House CZK 12,000 per project; Rest House CZK 6,000 per person; House in the Neighborhood CZK 30,000 per project; House of Sweat CZK 15,000 per project. All include workspace at Studio ALTA; the two production residencies add dramaturgic, production, technical and PR support. Free to apply.

Duration: Programme dependent: 5 to 10 days, at various points between February and November 2027

Deadline: 10 Sep 2026

Prague performance venue Studio ALTA announces four residency open calls for 2027, all with a single deadline of 10 September 2026. RESEARCH HOUSE (19 to 28 April 2027): a shared residential laboratory for three art projects or individual artists in the early stages of exploration and experimentation, or reopening an existing finished work (performance, installation, object, video) to transform it into another form such as a workshop, text or performance-lecture. Includes a 10-day residency, a fee of CZK 12,000 per project, shared studio, individual workspace and facilitated exchange meetings; the research output must be shared publicly as a work-in-progress in a form based on participants' needs. REST HOUSE (March to November 2027): a five-day residential spa for overloaded colleagues from the arts sector, with no required output or activities; restricted to people working in production, dramaturgy, curation, PR, technical and other supporting artistic professions in the Czech independent sector. Two guests are chosen by lottery (fee CZK 6,000 per person); the public draw is announced 16 September 2026. HOUSE IN THE NEIGHBORHOOD (9 to 18 August 2027): for one performative art project created with the local community and designed or adapted for public space in Liben and its surroundings; this year's call focuses on the 55+ target group. Includes a fee of CZK 30,000 per project, rehearsal and indoor facilities (primarily outdoor spaces), dramaturgic, production, technical and PR consultation, connections to partner organisations, and 7 days of intensive production and technical support in the final phase. A public premiere or work-in-progress in public space at the end of the residency is required. HOUSE OF SWEAT (1 to 10 February 2027): for one performative art project designed or adapted for the specific environment of the Studio ALTA sauna and its immediate surroundings, seeking new ways of working with intimate space, proximity to the audience and non-traditional formats. Includes a fee of CZK 15,000 per project, a 10-day residency, sauna and rehearsal spaces, dramaturgic, production, technical and PR consultation, and 2 days of intensive final-phase support; a public work-in-progress or premiere in the sauna within the 9 to 12 February 2027 programme block is required. Projects at any stage of development can apply to the production calls, and selected projects may be included in Studio ALTA's year-round programme. TIMELINE: deadline 10 September 2026; results 3 weeks after the deadline (30 September 2026); a Q&A Zoom call takes place 10 August 2026 at 3:00 PM. Apply via the registration forms on the call page.

item.title: Accion Cultural Espanola: PICE Visitantes 2026 (Phase 3)
item.description:
Organisation: Accion Cultural Espanola (AC/E)

Location: Spain. The host event must take place in Spain and the applicant must be constituted in Spain.

Award: Max EUR 20,000 per applicant per call, per event and per thematic area; within that, max EUR 2,000 per international visitor. Total 2026 call budget EUR 1,200,000 (Cine EUR 180,000, Artes visuales EUR 160,000, Musica y creacion sonora EUR 150,000, Literatura EUR 150,000, Arquitectura y diseno EUR 90,000, Podcast EUR 90,000, Videojuego y animacion EUR 90,000). No application fee.

Duration: Single event; Phase 3 visits must start on or after 1 November 2026 and finish before 28 February 2027.

Deadline: 07 Sep 2026

PICE Visitantes is the inbound mirror of PICE Movilidad: a Spanish festival, biennial, fair, museum or platform applies for AC/E to fund bringing international programmers, curators, producers and cultural professionals to its event in Spain, so that they meet Spanish artists and go on to programme them abroad. It is direct money to an organisation to enrich a festival or public programme it is already hosting. The same ten thematic areas apply as in Movilidad, including Artes visuales, Musica y creacion sonora, Podcast and Videojuego y animacion, giving good coverage for media-arts, sound-art and creative-technology events. Covered costs are travel, accommodation, travel insurance, internal transport, text translation and simultaneous or consecutive interpretation for the invited visitors, with the exact list varying slightly by thematic area. Only entities constituted in Spain may apply; natural persons are barred. Invited guests may come from any country including non-EU and the UK. TIMING: Phase 3 closes 7 September 2026, provisional list 21 October, definitive list 30 October, and visits may not start before 1 November 2026. Applications go through the AC/E PICE online system in Spanish or English with no fee.

item.title: Fondazione CRT: Orizzonti L.I.V.E. 2026 (second session)
item.description:
Organisation: Fondazione CRT (Fondazione Cassa di Risparmio di Torino)

Location: Piedmont and Valle d'Aosta, Italy. Activities must be delivered in those regions; the applicant does not itself have to be headquartered there.

Award: Max EUR 100,000 requestable. The project's own budget must be at least EUR 100,000. Mandatory co-financing of at least 70 percent of eligible project costs, so CRT covers a maximum of 30 percent. The requested amount is assessed against the applicant's last approved annual accounts and grant history. No application fee.

Duration: Project period set in the application; extensions of the grant-use deadline of up to 12 months may be requested.

Deadline: 15 Sep 2026

Orizzonti L.I.V.E. is Fondazione CRT's flagship thematic call for organisations that programme live performance as a driver of territorial transformation. The acronym stands for Luoghi, Impatto, Visioni, Energia, and stated priorities are strengthening organisations rooted in their territory, audience development reaching new publics, social inclusion and access for economically or socially fragile audiences, professional engagement of young musicians, actors and dancers, audience engagement aimed at under-25s, stable networks and strategic partnerships, and environmental sustainability aligned with Agenda 2030. This is festival and season funding at meaningful scale: the maximum request is EUR 100,000 and the overall project budget must itself be at least EUR 100,000, with co-financing covering at least 70 percent of eligible costs, so the applicant must bring roughly EUR 70,000 from other sources. The 2026 call runs in two sessions: the first closed 27 February 2026, and the second closes 15 September 2026 at 15:00 Italian time. Applications go through rol.fondazionecrt.it. SCOPE CAVEAT: this is broad live-performance funding rather than a media-arts line, so it fits experimental performance, sound art and hybrid live work but also covers conventional music and theatre. Non-EU and UK organisations can realistically only participate as project partners, not as lead applicants.

item.title: KNOWCASE Open Call 2027: permanent digital-culture installation in Madrid (Sonar+D x Fundacion Cotec)
item.description:
Organisation: Fundacion Cotec and Sonar+D

Location: Installation at the KNOWCASE storefront of Fundacion Cotec's headquarters in Chamberi, Madrid, Spain, a street-level venue visible 24/7. The call is international; applications accepted in Spanish, other official languages of Spain, or English.

Award: Up to EUR 100,000 (plus VAT), all-inclusive: conceptualisation, design, technical development, production, installation, maintenance, documentation, artist fees, travel, accommodation and insurance.

Duration: Installation displayed for a minimum of 24 months, starting February 2027

Deadline: 07 Sep 2026

Fundacion Cotec (a Spanish innovation-focused non-profit) and Sonar+D, building on an initial experiment at Sonar 2026, invite proposals for a long-term installation at KNOWCASE, the street-level showcase of Cotec's Madrid headquarters in Chamberi, visible to the public 24 hours a day. THEME: digital culture, meaning projects that combine knowledge, research, science and data with art, technology and social impact. Cotec's stated priorities are the big transitions (analogue to digital, linear to circular economy, tangible to intangible) plus innovation ecosystems and R&D&I, the climate crisis, the future of work and learning, social divides, citizen participation and democratic health. WHAT YOU GET: a budget of up to EUR 100,000 plus VAT covering everything (design, production, installation, maintenance, documentation, artist fees, travel, accommodation and insurance), and a minimum 24-month public display from February 2027. WHO CAN APPLY: artists, collectives, designers, technologists, universities, research centres, startups, businesses, creative agencies, producers, cultural institutions and multidisciplinary teams, internationally; applicants must demonstrate solid experience and a relevant portfolio. CONSTRAINTS: the proposal must be original and never previously exhibited, must include participative or interactive elements, must encourage critical thinking, and must be technically and financially viable for the full 24+ month exhibition period (durability and maintenance are central selection criteria). Selection weighs conceptual quality highest (40 percent), followed by public interactivity (25 percent). HOW TO APPLY: one PDF of maximum 15 pages containing summary, concept, technical proposal, visuals, budget, timeline, team profile, portfolio and declaration, in Spanish, another official language of Spain, or English, via the application portal linked from the terms and conditions. Results announced 14 October 2026. Deadline 7 September 2026 at midnight CEST.

item.title: Cultuurloket DigitALL: Pilot Contribution (Pilotbijdrage, 2026-2027, rolling)
item.description:
Organisation: Cultuurloket DigitALL (successor to Kickstart Cultuurfonds)

Location: Netherlands and the Caribbean parts of the Kingdom. No city or region restriction.

Award: Up to EUR 75,000. Covers pilot development, audience testing, and knowledge development or training via partner organisations if budgeted. Hardware-only purchases are not eligible. No stated co-financing percentage. No application fee. Annual donation budget of EUR 1.9 million in 2026 and 2027.

Duration: Not fixed; scoped to pilot, prototype or first live version development. Scheme runs through the end of 2027.

Deadline: Rolling / undated

Cultuurloket DigitALL funds the digital innovation of the Dutch cultural sector and is the strongest dedicated digital-culture route currently open to Dutch cultural organisations. It is the successor to the discontinued Kickstart Cultuurfonds, backed by the VandenEnde Foundation, VSBfonds, Ammodo, Het Cultuurfonds and others. The pilot contribution of up to EUR 75,000 supports developing and running a first pilot, prototype or live version of a digital tool, which covers a wide range of creative-technology work embedded in festivals, exhibitions and public programmes. Eligible applicants are theatres, music venues, film theatres, museums, festivals and professional performing arts producers, with collaborations between institutions given priority. The pilot must be tested with the intended public audience, not only with experts, and funding cannot be used exclusively for hardware acquisition. Applications go through an online portal with no deadline and are handled in order of receipt. TIMING: a decision follows within ten weeks of submission, so plan roughly three months of lead time between applying and project start. Training and knowledge development through partner organisations is only covered when included in the submitted budget, so build it in from the outset.

item.title: Brabant C: ASML x Brabant C Project Scheme (2026-2027, rolling)
item.description:
Organisation: Brabant C (Provincie Noord-Brabant culture investment fund) in partnership with ASML

Location: Noord-Brabant, Brainport-focused. Applicant must be based in the Brainport region (21 municipalities including Eindhoven, Helmond, Best) or in eight adjacent municipalities including Tilburg and Den Bosch, and the project must demonstrably benefit culture in the Brainport region. Province-restricted.

Award: EUR 25,000 minimum, up to EUR 500,000. Contribution capped at 50 percent of total project budget, so 50 percent co-financing is mandatory. EUR 1.7 million available per year, split evenly between ASML and Brabant C. Requests at or above EUR 50,000 must include a future-viability plan. No application fee.

Duration: Project-based, year-round intake via the AIMS portal.

Deadline: Rolling / undated

The closest thing the Netherlands has to a dedicated regional art-and-technology fund, being a public-private scheme co-financed by ASML and sited in the country's main technology region. It funds professional cultural projects of high quality with national or international reach, which in practice covers festivals, exhibitions and public programmes including media art and creative technology work. Private-law legal entities only (stichting, vereniging or BV); both new and existing cultural organisations qualify. Projects are assessed on societal impact (must address at least two of accessibility, inclusivity, diversity, social cohesion), cultural entrepreneurship and sustainability, alongside professional artistic quality. Applications are accepted all year round via a two-stage route: an intake where Brabant C scouts give an initial assessment, followed by a full application, pitch session and decision. TIMING RULES ARE STRICT and are the main planning constraint: the full application must be submitted a minimum of 12 weeks before the project starts, and the project may not begin until at least 12 weeks after a complete application has been approved. The internal clock runs roughly two weeks for a completeness check, about six weeks to the pitch session, and about four weeks from pitch to decision. Brabant C never covers more than half the budget, so a matched partner is required from the outset. A separate Brabant C matching scheme for impactful culture projects is open year-round through 31 December 2026 for Brabant-based organisations outside the Brainport region.

item.title: Refusing Rehearsing Resisting: VBKÖ Annual Programme Open Call 2027-2028
item.description:
Organisation: VBKÖ (Vereinigung bildender Künstler*innen Österreichs, Austrian Association of Wom*n Artists)

Location: Vienna, Austria (VBKÖ exhibition spaces and shared kitchen)

Award: EUR 4,000 total budget per selected project, covering both artist fees and production costs (fees, materials, labour, production, transport and other project expenses). Participants based outside Vienna must include travel, accommodation and shipping within that budget or secure external funding; VBKÖ provides invitation and support letters to help raise additional money. Also provided: the spaces and shared kitchen, graphic design of online promotional material, press announcements, photo documentation, up to 10 hours of technical setup support, and technical equipment. Installation and de-installation are the selected group's responsibility. No application fee.

Duration: 4 to 6 weeks, taking place between March 2027 and February 2028

Deadline: 10 Sep 2026

VBKÖ, the Austrian Association of Wom*n Artists founded in 1910, invites proposals for its annual programme running March 2027 to February 2028. The call reads the present moment through the resurgence of authoritarianism, fascism, militarisation, colonial violence and extractive capitalism, and the parallel privatisation of care and criminalisation of solidarity. Drawing on María Galindo's framing of feminism as a project of social transformation and Sara Ahmed's account of feminist work beginning with refusal, the programme treats alternative ways of living as something rehearsed collectively through organising, creating, caring, listening, remembering and struggling. VBKÖ seeks a programme of practices that nurture communal care and build a platform for collective rehearsals: proposals that allow for tenderness, that are not afraid of ugly feelings and different truths, and that explore how contemporary queer and feminist perspectives resonate across artistic, social and political movements. FORMAT REQUIREMENT: only exhibition formats bringing together multiple artists, collectives or collaborative practices are accepted. Solo exhibitions, individual presentations and projects centred on a single artist's work are explicitly not supported. Proposals that activate the exhibition through public programming (screenings, performances, workshops, lectures and other events) are encouraged. Regular opening hours are Fridays and Saturdays 2pm to 6pm; any additional hours must be arranged and staffed by the selected group. The association acknowledges that its own history is marked by violence, exclusion and discrimination on the basis of religion, class, gender, sexuality and ethnicity, and states that it actively opposes all forms of discrimination including trans-exclusionary radical feminism. APPLICATION: a single PDF (max 5MB) with a programme description (max 2 pages, images welcome, English or German, including preferred dates and duration), a CV and biography for every participant (max 1 page each), a financial plan (Fair Pay encouraged), technical requirements, and contact details including email, mobile number and main residence; three high-resolution images of work or exhibition sketches sent within the email or via a download link, labelled with artist name, work title, year and proposal title (video links may be included in the proposal). Send to opencall@vbkoe.org with the subject line 'Open Call + your proposal title'. Incomplete applications will not be considered. A shortlist is compiled by the VBKÖ team and final selections are made by the VBKÖ board with an external jury member experienced in contemporary art, activism and community building; shortlisted applicants may be asked to present to the jury. Results are announced at the beginning of October 2026. Deadline 10 September 2026, 23:59. Free to apply.

item.title: Fucina Futura 2027 Residency (Marostica, Italy)
item.description:
Organisation: Futura Association (Fucina Futura), supported by Culture Moves Europe

Location: Marostica, Italy (one hour from Venice). Open to artists resident in a Creative Europe country except Italy.

Award: Fully funded: daily fee to cover living expenses, travel costs covered, and shared house accommodation provided (supported by Culture Moves Europe). No application fee.

Duration: One month, 12 April to 12 May 2027; three residents hosted together

Deadline: Closed 20 Aug 2026

Fucina Futura is an artist residency in Marostica, a small town about an hour from Venice, offering a peaceful setting to develop research in close contact with nature and the local community. The project spans two locations: the home designed by internationally renowned illustrator Elena Xausa near the historic centre, and the atelier Fucina Ai Gorghi by beloved local painter Daniele Marcon, ideal for large-scale installations. Led by visual artist Lavinia and curator Sofia (Futura Association), the program invites residents to develop projects that engage with the community and the working location, and encourages artists of any discipline to make full use of the large atelier. The central goal is the 'restitution' to citizens, fostering cultural exchange and community inclusion: this final phase is tailored to each artist and can take the form of an exhibition, performance, workshop, screening, talk or informal sharing session, prioritising direct dialogue with the public and the contemporary renewal of local tradition. THREE residents are hosted together from 12 April to 12 May 2027 and share a spacious house; they receive a daily fee to cover living expenses, and travel expenses are also covered. Made possible by Culture Moves Europe. ELIGIBILITY: only artists residing in one of the Creative Europe countries EXCEPT ITALY may apply. Creative Europe covers the 27 EU member states (other than Italy), plus Albania, Armenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Iceland, Kosovo, Liechtenstein, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Norway, Serbia, Tunisia and Ukraine, and includes the EU's Overseas Countries and Territories and Outermost Regions (Greenland; French Guiana, French Polynesia, French Southern and Antarctic Territories, Guadeloupe, Martinique, Mayotte, New Caledonia, Reunion, Saint Barthelemy, Saint-Martin, St. Pierre and Miquelon, Wallis and Futuna; Azores, Madeira; Canary Islands; Aruba, Bonaire, Curacao, Saba, Sint Maarten, Sint Eustatius). TIMELINE: apply via the Google Form by 20 August 2026; selected artists informed by 30 August and must confirm participation by 8 September 2026.

item.title: Gemeente Den Haag: Arts and Culture Projects Category B (autumn 2026 round)
item.description:
Organisation: Gemeente Den Haag (Municipality of The Hague)

Location: The Hague. Applicant must be active in Den Haag and the project must be publicly accessible there. City-restricted.

Award: EUR 10,000 to 30,000 per application. The municipal culture-budget contribution may not exceed 30 percent of the total project budget, so at least 70 percent co-financing is required. Annual ceiling for the strand is EUR 600,000. No application fee.

Duration: Maximum one year per project.

Deadline: 15 Oct 2026

The larger of The Hague's two municipal project bands and the appropriate route for an organisation running a festival or substantial public programme in the city. Awards range from EUR 10,000 to 30,000 against an annual ceiling of EUR 600,000 for the whole strand. THE CO-FINANCING REQUIREMENT IS SEVERE and is the single most important planning constraint: the municipal culture budget may fund at most 30 percent of the total project budget, so an applicant seeking EUR 30,000 must already have roughly EUR 70,000 secured or plausibly projected elsewhere. Only legal entities may apply; individuals and informal collectives must use Category A instead (EUR 2,000 to 10,000, 70 percent coverage ceiling, next window 1 to 15 September 2026). Professional arts and culture organisations running public projects in music, theatre, dance, film, literature, visual arts or combinations are eligible. The next window opens 1 October and closes at 17:00 on 15 October 2026. TIMING: the decision term is 12 weeks after the window closes, so an October 2026 application is decided around early January 2027 and activity should be scheduled from 2027 onward. Applications are handled through the municipality's subsidy system, which migrated to Easyfunders in April 2026. This scheme is independent of Stroom Den Haag. The underlying regulation runs to 31 December 2028.

item.title: Stichting NORMA: NORMA Fonds Project Grant (round 4, 2026)
item.description:
Organisation: Stichting NORMA (collecting society for performing artists)

Location: Netherlands-based arts-sector activity. No city or region restriction stated.

Award: Maximum EUR 10,000 per project. Total project budget may not exceed EUR 150,000 and the applicant organisation's annual budget may not exceed EUR 500,000. At least 25 percent of the project budget must come from audience or box-office revenue. Performer fees must meet the 2026 wage norms of EUR 139 per rehearsal and EUR 340 per performance. No application fee.

Duration: Single project, typically a production or concert series. Final report due within six months of completion.

Deadline: 30 Oct 2026

The NORMA Fonds redistributes copyright remuneration collected by Stichting NORMA into cultural, social and professional projects involving performing artists, and is one of the few Dutch schemes with four intakes a year and a genuinely short cycle. Both arts-sector organisations and individual arts professionals may apply, though the applicant needs a bank account and legal footing and cannot be a BIS-funded institution. The project must centre on performing artists in the copyright sense, meaning people who perform a copyright-protected work: musicians, dancers, actors, voice actors. This fits live experimental music, sound performance and performative media-art work, but not object-based exhibitions or non-performative installation programmes. The maximum grant is EUR 10,000, the total project budget must stay under EUR 150,000, the applicant's annual budget under EUR 500,000, and at least a quarter of the project budget must be earned from audience income, so this is a top-up rather than a primary funding source. Budgets must honour NORMA's 2026 performer wage norms. Applications are submitted online during a one-month window each quarter; the next round runs 1 to 30 October 2026, closing at 23:59. TIMING RULE: decisions arrive no later than eight weeks after the deadline, and the premiere date must fall at least eight weeks after the application deadline. Organisations that already received a NORMA Fonds grant in 2024 or 2025 are excluded, and supporting staff may not exceed 2 FTE.

item.title: University of Amsterdam: PhD, Protest and Political Speech in the Nordics 1930-1970 (Sound of Disagreement)

Location: Amsterdam, Netherlands (Kloveniersburgwal 48)

Award: EUR 3,059 to 3,881 gross per month at 38 hours per week, on the Dutch university PhD scale, plus 8 percent holiday allowance and 8.3 percent year-end bonus. No application fee.

Duration: 48 months full-time (16-month initial contract, extended by 32 months after a positive evaluation); preferred start 1 January 2027

Deadline: Closed 20 Aug 2026

Fully funded four-year PhD position within 'The Sound of Disagreement: Embodied Histories of Political Speech 1800-present', an interdisciplinary project on how political groups have argued in public and how disagreement sounds. This sub-project covers Nordic labour movements and the articulation of protest from roughly 1930 to 1970, explicitly working on the sonic practices of political debate and the mediatization of protest, so it suits researchers with a sound studies, media studies or oral history angle as much as historians. REQUIREMENTS: a master's degree in History, European Studies, Media Studies, Nordic Studies or a related discipline; fluency in Danish, Finnish, Norwegian or Swedish depending on the chosen case study; professional English; archival research skills; and a collaborative disposition. item.title: Fonds Podiumkunsten: Foreign Performances or Concerts in the Netherlands (round 4, 2026)

Location: Activity must take place in the Netherlands. Applicants from Aruba, Bonaire, Curacao, Sint Maarten, Saba and Sint Eustatius are also in scope. No city or region restriction.

Award: Maximum EUR 25,000 per production, capped at EUR 75,000 for an applicant presenting multiple productions. Calculated on travel and transport costs of the foreign artists and their production only. EUR 267,500 available per round shared across this scheme and two sibling internationalisation schemes. Fees, venue and production costs stay with the applicant. No application fee.

Duration: Single performances or a short run of concerts within one programme or festival edition.

Deadline: 23 Sep 2026

Fonds Podiumkunsten's route for Dutch festivals and venues bringing in exceptional foreign performing arts and concerts that Dutch audiences would otherwise not see. The applicant must be a Netherlands-registered legal entity running a venue or festival and carrying artistic and financial responsibility for its own programme, so individuals and sole traders cannot apply. Grants are calculated from travel and transport costs of the incoming artists, at a maximum of EUR 25,000 per production and EUR 75,000 per applicant across several productions. The core test is that the foreign work is rarely or never seen in the Netherlands and substantially enriches the existing Dutch offer, which favours experimental, non-canonical and cross-disciplinary programming over mainstream touring. Experimental music and sound-art programming is not excluded; the selection criterion is rarity and added value, not genre. Applications go through the Mijn Fonds portal and there is no fee. Four rounds run each year. TIMING: because the scheme competes against a shared EUR 267,500 per-round pot and assessment takes several weeks after the deadline, organisers should apply at least one full round ahead of the performance date and must not have the activity already underway. item.title: Stichting Cultuur Eindhoven: Project Subsidy (Projecten, 2027 round 1)
item.description:
Organisation: Stichting Cultuur Eindhoven

Location: Eindhoven. The applicant must be a legal entity based in Eindhoven and the activity must serve the Eindhoven cultural offering. City-restricted at the applicant level.

Award: Maximum EUR 35,000 per application and maximum 80 percent of eligible costs, so at least 20 percent co-financing is required. No application fee.

Duration: Single project within the 2025-2028 policy period.

Deadline: 30 Sep 2026

The mid-size project strand of Stichting Cultuur Eindhoven, the arm's-length body that distributes the city's culture budget, and the main municipal route for an Eindhoven organisation to fund a festival, exhibition or public programme. Awards go up to EUR 35,000 and cover a maximum of 80 percent of eligible costs, so at least a fifth of the budget must come from elsewhere. Unlike the Snelgeld strand this route is closed to individuals: only private-law legal entities established in Eindhoven may apply. item.title: Privacy Camp 2026 (EDRi): Call for Sessions, The Origins of Future Technologies
item.description:
Organisation: European Digital Rights (EDRi), with LSTS at Vrije Universiteit Brussel, Privacy Salon vzw, the Institute for European Studies at Université Saint-Louis Bruxelles, and the Racism and Technology Center

Location: Brussels, Belgium, and online (hybrid). Event on 13 October 2026.

Award: NO speaker fee or honorarium. Where needed, up to EUR 400 per speaker or session organiser towards transport to and accommodation in Brussels, reimbursed against invoices and travel tickets; those with organisational support are encouraged to cover their own expenses. No budget beyond this cap. Free to propose and free to attend (registration open).

Duration: One-day conference on 13 October 2026. Average session length 50 minutes.

Deadline: Closed 10 Aug 2026

Privacy Camp holds its 14th edition on 13 October 2026 in Brussels and online, organised by European Digital Rights (EDRi) with the Research Group on Law, Science, Technology & Society (LSTS) at Vrije Universiteit Brussel, Privacy Salon vzw, the Institute for European Studies at Université Saint-Louis Bruxelles, and the Racism and Technology Center. THEME: 'The Origins of Future Technologies: Towards communities of digital self-determination'. The call starts from the premise that digital futures do not appear from nowhere but are built through land, labour, capital, infrastructure, law, public money, political choices and social struggle, and asks where technologies come from, who gets to shape them, and what conditions make digital self-determination possible. It situates this against the EU's 2026 Tech Sovereignty Package (semiconductors, artificial intelligence, cloud infrastructure and data centres) and the wider deregulatory agenda including the Digital Omnibus, the AI Omnibus and reforms affecting data protection, privacy, labour and environmental safeguards, asking whose version of sovereignty is actually being discussed. TOPIC AREAS: (1) Material conditions in the production of technologies, covering the natural resources needed across the supply chain (critical components such as semiconductors, water for data centres) and how GDPR, ePrivacy and AI Act safeguards shape the material conditions of AI from data extraction and biometric processing through to data centres, labour and public infrastructure; labour conditions, including who mines critical materials, union-busting across the tech supply chain, and coalitions between tech workers, unions, migrant justice groups, climate movements and digital rights organisations; and capital, meaning the venture capital forces driving the current AI hype and consolidating through defence, security and militarisation. (2) Political vision in the use of technologies, covering military use and how militarisation and securitisation shape the EU deregulation debate, and the political ideologies driving technology development, including what digital self-determination means for communities facing racialised discrimination, surveillance, occupation, border violence, workplace control or environmental harm. (3) Moving technologies forward through communities, covering community innovation for digital self-determination (distributed and self-hosted data storage, AI built by and for community needs, community-led, public or cooperative digital infrastructure); law, deregulation and rights (resisting the Digital Omnibus and specifically the Data Omnibus, defending GDPR and ePrivacy safeguards, protecting access, transparency and automated decision-making rights, enforcing existing digital laws, supporting collective litigation, and challenging the framing of rights as obstacles to EU competitiveness); and building power by connecting grassroots movements across tech worker organising, labour, migrant, LGBTQIA+, climate, economic justice and landback movements. FORMATS: interactive workshops are particularly encouraged, meaning small-group work, peer exchange and collaboration across sectors, coalitions and disciplines, moving from talk to strategic action; panel discussions are also welcome, especially those centring diverse voices and grounded lived experience with room for meaningful audience engagement. SUBMISSION GUIDELINES: state a clear objective for the session and what a good outcome would be; make it as interactive as possible; support a diversity of voices and multiple perspectives; average session length is 50 minutes; propose the format that actually suits the idea rather than forcing a panel into a workshop or vice versa. For workshops, make the objectives, structure and facilitation clear and have participants work together in small groups towards a specific goal; the organisers provide additional guidance, support and feedback for workshops. For panels, list a maximum of 4 speakers covering academia, civil society and decision-maker perspectives, and indicate which speakers have confirmed at least in principle. TIMELINE: proposals due via the online form by 10 August 2026 at 09:00 CEST; the Content Committee notifies applicants before 21 August 2026; confirmation to proceed required by 25 August; draft programme published 4 September; speakers and final session description confirmed by 10 September at the latest (earlier confirmation improves the odds that the EUR 400 reimbursement budget covers speaker travel and accommodation); final programme published 28 September. The 2026 Content Committee is Andreea Belu (EDRi), Gloria González Fuster (LSTS, VUB), Jill Toh (Racism and Technology Center), Sanne Stevens (Justice, Equity and Technology Project) and Alexandra Giannopoulou (DFF). Programme enquiries: andreea.belu@edri.org. Venue and reimbursement enquiries: guillermo.peris@edri.org.
